recent_commits.message: Unpack only kept archive files within max_file_size in data_check (0.3.3.14)
recent_commits.body:
- .archive_keep(): the keep rule of .archive_rows() (data, code, README and
  codebook documentation, not skip_types or useless files), applied to an
  archive's listing before anything is unpacked
- .expand_compressed() decompresses a .gz/.bz2/.xz only when the inner file
  is kept, and stops at max_bytes (partial copy deleted); .expand_zip() and
  .expand_tar() unpack only kept members within max_bytes (sizes from the
  zip listing or tar headers; a compressed tar's are checked after
  unpacking). Files over the limit are listed without a copy and added to
  data_check's oversize record; copies over the limit from earlier runs are
  removed (#472)
- .rate_limit_wait test allows a few seconds instead of an exact rounded 900
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: power: free-text categories mapped onto known values, report unchecked paragraphs, require ellmer 0.4.2 (0.3.3.13)
recent_commits.body:
- The LLM answers power_type, statistical_test, effect_size_metric and
  software as free strings; .power_canonicalise() maps them onto the known
  values, keeping an unmatched answer in *_other (new software_other). A
  value outside a type_enum() made Groq reject the whole call (POWSIM)
- The software list holds 116 power/sample-size packages from CRAN's
  package list, 10 widely used ones whose title does not say so, 6 no longer
  on CRAN or from Bioconductor, and other software (POWSIM, nQuery, SAS, ...)
- Paragraphs the LLM could not check are counted and reported (summary,
  report, yellow light, power_unchecked per paper) instead of being counted
  as having no power analysis
- DESCRIPTION: ellmer (>= 0.4.2)
- The Ollama structured power test also replaces ellmer::chat_vllm(), used
  since #494 (#475)
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Follow Dryad sharing links, report GitHub accounts, OSF registration licences, README and GeoTIFF classification, list plain .tar archives (0.3.3.9)
recent_commits.body:
- Dryad: a sharing link (datadryad.org/stash/share/...) is resolved to its
  DOI with one request; one that leads nowhere is reported as a private or
  expired sharing link. Dryad metadata uses .col_chr() and each link's own
  error reaches gated_repos (Dryad part of #476) (#484)
- GitHub: an account or organisation address is reported as an account,
  not as an invalid repository; github_links() keeps such links; a
  repository name of only dots is not looked up. GitLab single-segment
  addresses likewise (#485)
- OSF: .osf_license() and .osf_node_metadata() read /registrations/<id>/
  after a 404 from /nodes/; with osf_license = TRUE, repo_check looks up the
  licence of the project a cited registration was made from, falling back
  to the registration's own (#486)
- README detection: read.me is a README name (one rule shared by
  file_category, repo_check and code_check); text documents named "data"
  are documentation; "Data description" files get the README role (#487)
- A plain .tar of known size up to 50 MB is downloaded once and listed from
  its headers (ustar, pax and GNU long names); data_check takes members from
  the session copy without another request (#487, plain-tar part of #444)
- GeoTIFF rasters next to GIS files are data; world files, overviews, GDAL
  sidecars, NetCDF, raster grids, band files, virtual rasters and KML/KMZ
  are data by extension (#488)
- .csv_is_space_separated() no longer warns for a missing file

recent_commits.message: Fix self-hosted bibr, Qwen 3 on Ollama, and the app's repository switch (0.3.3.9)
recent_commits.body:
- convert(method = "bibr") passes its arguments to convert_bibr() (#489)
- convert_bibr(backend = "selfhosted") sends a bearer token (api_key or
  BIBR_API_KEY), defaults to BIBR_API_URL, and honours timeout (#490)
- .bibr_isalive() accepts bibr serve's own /ready answer (#491)
- report_app(): call .grobid_isalive() as metacheck:::.grobid_isalive() (#493)
- Structured calls to Qwen 3 on Ollama send reasoning_effort = "none" and go
  through ellmer's OpenAI-compatible provider, so extractions no longer run
  out of tokens or skip optional fields (#494)
- shiny_app: unticking "Query Data Repositories" also skips prereg_check,

recent_commits.message: Stop the quadratic rescan of rejected blocks in .r_output_tables() (0.3.3.8)
recent_commits.body:
A printed data frame with no numeric column made every row start a new
scan of the rest of the print, so parsing console output grew with the
square of the rows (384 s for 1,000 rows, hours for 10,000). A rejected
block is now remembered: a later start inside it is only split when its
pattern of non-blank character positions differs from the last block
actually split, the only way its result can differ. Output is identical
on 113 cases; 1,000 rows take about 4 s. A progress line is printed
before each script's output is parsed.

Closes #483
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Keep one copy of each function defined twice in R/ (0.3.3.7)
recent_commits.body:
Eleven internal functions and one constant were defined twice; R loads R/
alphabetically, so one copy silently replaced the other. Kept: R/stat_helpers.R
for the nine statistics helpers and .STAT_PLACEHOLDERS (the file created as
their single home), omv.R for .html_inline_images(), reproducibility_check.R
for .repro_split_args(). All copies were identical, so behaviour is unchanged.
Each deleted copy leaves a one-line pointer to the kept one. New test fails
when any name is defined twice.

Closes #482
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Stop the quadratic character walks that hung reproducibility_check (0.3.3.6)
recent_commits.body:
Every place that walked text one character at a time with substr(x, i, i)
now splits the text into characters once and indexes the vector. For text
with a non-ASCII character substr() counts from the start on every call, so
the walk was quadratic: 201 s for a 200,000-character script, hours for a
1-MB one. Results are identical on 413 real R and Python scripts.

Changed: .repro_redirect_writes(), .repro_format_call_refs(),
.repro_split_args() (both copies), .repro_content_sniff(),
.r_call_object_ref(), .omv_extract_syntax(), .smcl_render_line().
repro_write_scripts() prints a line per script, so a slow rewrite can be
told apart from a hang.

Closes #481
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Follow-up fixes to #479 in reproducibility_check, code_check, data_check and codebook_check (0.3.3.5)
recent_commits.body:
- NEWS: restore the 12 sub-items (0.2.0 and the bib/xrefs entries) that a
  search-and-replace in 9509af1 had prefixed; list the data_check changes
  from the data_validate merge that were never in NEWS
- reproducibility_check: replace setwd()/os.chdir() with a no-op
  (invisible(NULL) / pass) instead of commenting it out, which left Python
  blocks empty (IndentationError) and gave an R `if` the next statement as
  its body; say when processx is missing instead of "no Python interpreter";
  name the current Docker image; say "Docker container" when Docker runs
- code_check: label a notebook Python only for a Python kernel (Julia and
  other kernels get their own language, none when undeclared), Julia Quarto
  documents no longer R; read the language from the downloaded file, since
  the file name alone labelled every notebook Python and every Quarto
  document R
- data_check: careless responding per file and respondent; block (not file)
  minimum of 5 items; yellow light when data files were found but none could
  be read; report and comments no longer name checks that do not run;
  verb agreement in spreadsheet findings
- codebook_check: values are checked only against a documented range;
  data_check_scale_values() gains `infer`
- tests for all of the above and for the space-separated .csv check

Closes #480

recent_commits.message: Leave out and report all files that do not belong in a repository
recent_commits.body:
Extends the operating-system file filter to every file software creates by
itself that holds nothing a reader can use: operating-system files (macOS,
Windows, Linux desktops), RStudio's .Rproj.user/, Jupyter checkpoints,
compiled Python files and Office/LibreOffice lock files. Patterns from
GitHub's ignore-file templates, each also found in real repositories; files
that may matter (.RData, .Rhistory, backups, *.tmp, knitr caches) are kept.

repo_check and data_check leave them out of the file list; repo_check reports
them by kind in "Files that do not belong in the repository". The kind is
taken from the last path segment without basename(), which expanded a leading
"~" ("~$report.docx" became "Documents$report.docx").
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Support LDbase in repo_check; leave out operating-system files; warn on firewall browser checks (0.3.3.4)
recent_commits.body:
LDbase (ldbase.org, FSU's repository for educational and developmental
sciences) has no API, so the new ldbase_links()/ldbase_info() read its public
pages: links to projects, datasets, code and documents and 10.33009 DOIs are
found; a project's whole hierarchy (child projects included) is listed, each
item's current file in a folder named after the item, with the licence of
each item. Files download without an account. Pages are requested at most
once per second. Checked on 10 LDbase projects.

repo_check and data_check leave out files the operating system adds
(__MACOSX/, ._ files, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) and repo_check lists
them for the authors to remove: in one LDbase zip they were 993 of 1,826
listed files, and the ._ copies of .csv files were read as data.

A host's AWS WAF browser check (HTTP 202 + x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) now
gives a warning once per host; such files used to be skipped without a word
because their size could not be read.

DOIs under 10.33009 are no longer also looked up by dspace7_links();
open_practices counts "LDbase" as a repository word.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Python support fixes in reproducibility_check, %>% from other scripts, data_check and repo_check fixes (0.3.3.3)
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check (#479):
- Compare reported statistics with the analysis output once, after the R and
  the Python code, so Python output is included; Python-only papers keep the
  SPSS/Stata, self-reproducible-output and other-language sections and the
  SPSS/Stata red light
- Extract the code of Python notebooks and Quarto documents (and R-kernel
  notebooks) before running it
- Check Python syntax with ast.parse(); fall back to python3; report Python
  files as not run, instead of stopping, when no interpreter is found
- Install packages under their pip name (sklearn -> scikit-learn, ...)
- Require callr only for R code; drop the Python NameError re-run
- Return the summary as one text (two made the report error for R + Python)
- Stop exporting .repro_py_defined_vars(); correct help text and comments

R scripts that fail on %>% because packages are loaded in another script:
- A script another script runs with source() is only run inside that script
  (outcome run_by_source)
- Otherwise the re-run adds the library() calls of the project's other
  scripts, else the one package that exports the function, else magrittr;
  recorded in modifications and reported as reproducible after repair

Comparison with the paper: use the output's STATO type when a value's name is
not recognised (scipy's statistic/pvalue); type F_onewayResult,
PearsonRResult and Chi2ContingencyResult

data_check: warn on space-separated .csv files; keep the summary, report and
light when no table is readable (and return the column table as `table`);
read only the header line in the trial-level check (#477)

repo_check: ignore CI/service configuration files when deciding whether a
root-level R package is the deposit (#469)

reproducibility_check(workers > 1): copy all metacheck.* options into each
background process (#474)

check_file_naming(): help no longer lists case rules it does not check

Closes #479
Closes #474
Closes #477
Closes #469

- data_check's summary in a brief or simple_brief report no longer says how

recent_commits.body:
- OSF: list a project's whole component tree with its storage providers in

- Dryad and DSpace 7 listings no longer stop at 20 files; Dryad SHA-256

recent_commits.message: Add a Shiny Server app that checks a code and data repository
recent_commits.body:
Runs only repo_check, code_check and data_check, without a manuscript, on
either a link to an online repository (fetched by the server, nothing
uploaded) or an uploaded .zip of a local folder. Uploads, unpacked size,
file count, concurrent jobs and free disk space are capped so the shared
server cannot fill up, and each job's files are deleted when it ends.

recent_commits.message: Fetch Dryad zip members by downloading the archive once (#471)
recent_commits.body:
Fetching members by byte range costs two requests per member, which
exhausts Dryad's daily request limit on corpus runs. .zip_fetch_members()
gains a whole-archive mode: when at least 3 members are wanted and the
archive (size estimated from its central directory) fits the budget, it
downloads the archive once, keeps it on disk for restarted runs, and
extracts the wanted members locally; anything not delivered falls back to
the per-member fetch. Enabled only for datadryad.org archives, in

recent_commits.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
recent_commits.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Attribute #86 to GRIMMER in the unround.R header comment
recent_commits.body: * GRIM never derived its candidate sums from floating-point products; it rounded the two nearest granules forward and compared them with a tolerance, so its released versions were not affected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check needed columns in audit() and grim_plot(); fall back to rounding
recent_commits.body:
* Mapper output keeps its class after columns are dropped, so audit() and
  grim_plot() failed with unclear errors. A shared check_cols_needed() now
  names the missing columns; grim_plot_rates() and debit_plot() use it too.
* grim_plot() uses its rounding argument when data has no recorded
  rounding method, as with a hand-built tibble.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Map grim_plot() value-set colors to a scale and drop four style arguments
recent_commits.body:
* consistency is mapped to colour and fill of the value-set tiles, with one default scale for both, as in debit_plot(); adding another scale restyles them.
* color_cons, color_incons, tile_alpha, and raster_alpha are removed. tile_size and raster_color stay: no scale reaches them, and raster_color also builds the gradient for three or more decimal places.
* The in-depth vignette's plotting requirements now describe the scale instead of color arguments.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test check_audit_special() and manage_helper_col()
recent_commits.body:
* Both are exported for handwritten mappers but had no tests of their own.
* check_audit_special() is tested on basic, seq, and total-n output; manage_helper_col() on a column, an argument, the default, affix = FALSE, and the conflict error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Map debit_plot() colors to a scale and drop its fixed-style arguments
recent_commits.body:
* consistency is mapped to colour and fill, with one default scale_colour_manual() for both, so adding another scale restyles the plot.
* color_cons, color_incons, rect_alpha, and the line_* and label_* arguments are removed; their values are now constants. The pointless theme_update() call is gone too.
* A test checks the default colors and their replacement by a user's scale; the example shows how.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove seq_endpoint(), seq_distance(), their *_df() versions, and seq_test_ranking()
recent_commits.body:
* They produced sequences of decimal strings for testing with the mappers, which no longer accept strings, so their default output failed there. Their essence is seq(from, to, by = 10^-digits).
* The "scrutiny" attribute loses name_test and seq_test, which only seq_test_ranking() read.
* Tests of other functions build their input with seq() piped into round() instead, and the devtools vignette covers only seq_disperse(). The GRIM oracle test pipes into round() as well.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Quiet the 0.6.1 install script and use a tibble in the benchmark
recent_commits.body: * install_scrutiny_0_6_1() tries CRAN's current packages before the archive and keeps the expected 404 from the other location quiet.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave the factory arguments out of the disabled-argument error
recent_commits.body: * Users of grimmer_map() and the like were told about .args_disabled and .args_fixed, which only matter to whoever created the mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: List the removed mapper arguments and columns as breaking changes in NEWS
recent_commits.body: * The removal of debit_map(show_rec), grimmer_map(show_reason), debit_map()'s rounding column, and audit()'s fail_test2 moves from "Lifecycle updates" to "Function interfaces".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Mark the percentage and sum tests as experimental
recent_commits.body: * is_percentage_of(), is_percentage_of_map(), is_percentage_of_map_seq(), add_up_to(), and add_up_to_map() carry the experimental badge, and NEWS and the vignette say so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Hide the library(scrutiny) chunk and the header rule in vignettes
recent_commits.body:
* Every vignette still loads scrutiny, but in a chunk with include = FALSE.
* Article pages have no rule between the title and the text.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Correct NEWS claims and a stale comment from the recent cuts
recent_commits.body:
* GRIM's verdicts are unchanged only on testable value sets; untestable ones are now NA.
* .args_defaults never shipped, so NEWS no longer says it was replaced, and grim_map()'s items entry no longer claims the other mappers already kept n and items apart, which was only true of the dev version.
* A comment in grim_plot() still assumed grimmer_map() could omit the reason column.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a grim_plot_rates() study column named like a summary column
recent_commits.body: * A study column named observed, expected, value_sets, or ratio was overwritten by summarise(), so the study labels were lost without an error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check that function_map(.args_fixed) is a named list that overlaps nothing
recent_commits.body: * An unnamed value was passed to .fun by position, and a name shared with a by-row, helper, or disabled argument silently dropped that argument. Only overlap with key arguments was rejected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop tolerance from grimmer_plot_values()
recent_commits.body:
* It passed tolerance to grimmer() on every call, so since grimmer(tolerance) was deprecated, each call warned. The function is new in 1.0.0, so the argument goes without a deprecation.
* The no-warnings test missed this because a deprecation warns once per session and an earlier test had used it up. It now sets lifecycle_verbosity = "warning".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the logo out of the first code chunk on pkgdown pages
recent_commits.body:
* The page header contains the right-floated logo, so the logo no longer hangs below the header line into the first code chunk.
* Copy buttons are always shown, faintly until hovered, instead of appearing only on hover.
* The copy tooltip opens to the left of the button, as pkgdown intends; it opened above it and covered the logo because Bootstrap 5 ignores pkgdown's Bootstrap 4 placement attribute.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Bring docs in line with the cut features
recent_commits.body:
* ?grim_map_seq no longer says that n is the sample size before multiplying in items, which no mapper does anymore.
* The pkgdown reference lists duplicate_detect() under "Deprecated" rather than "Superseded".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Document the new tests and GRIM study-level tools in vignettes
recent_commits.body:
* A new vignette, "Percentages and sums", covers is_percentage_of() and add_up_to() with their mappers and audit() summaries.
* The GRIM vignette gains grim_plot_values() next to grim_plot(), and grim_binomial(), grim_binomial_power(), and grim_plot_rates() under GRIM statistics.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut the §2 dead weight and deprecate duplicate_detect()
recent_commits.body:
* Remove grim_ratio(), manage_key_colnames(), unnest_consistency_cols(), write_doc_factory_map_conventions(), and the rlang re-exports; unexport check_factory_dots(), check_args_disabled(), and decimal_places_scalar().
* Replace function_map(.args_defaults) by .args_fixed: values the factory-made function always passes on without exposing the argument. debit_map() loses show_rec and grimmer_map() loses show_reason; both outputs are always complete. debit_map() output loses its rounding column, which repeated the attribute, and audit() on GRIMMER output loses fail_test2, which could no longer be nonzero.
* duplicate_detect() warns with lifecycle; forensic_metascience calls it, so it stays for one more release.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rewrite the handwritten-mapper section around the kept helpers
recent_commits.body: * The examples use absorb_key_args() for renaming key columns, which replaces the reference to manage_key_colnames(), and the requirements describe helper columns as returned rather than merged.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Stop multiplying items into n in grim_map() and grimmer_map()
recent_commits.body:
* A helper column is now returned as itself, right after the key columns, if it was given as an argument or a column. The n column is the sample size as given.
* This removes function_map(.cols_helper_merge), the scrutiny_cols_helper_merge attribute, and the code in function_map_seq() and function_map_total_n() that undid the merge before re-testing. grim_plot() already placed tiles at n * items.
* Breaking change for grim_map() and grimmer_map() output with items > 1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop GRIMMER's test 2 and deprecate grimmer(tolerance)
recent_commits.body:
* Test 1 derives the admissible sums of squares from exact integer bounds that are the inverse of the SD's rounding, so every integer between them rounds back to the reported SD. Test 2 re-rounded each of them anyway, with a floating-point tolerance that could only lose matches.
* The parity test now needs no enumeration: two or more admissible integers include both parities, and a single one is compared to the sum. GRIMMER_CHUNK_SIZE goes with the loop.
* A sweep of 9,000 random cases over every rounding method, symmetric, items, and scale bounds gives the same verdicts and reasons as before. "GRIMMER inconsistent (test 2)" is no longer a possible reason.
* tolerance is deprecated the way grim()'s is.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
_new_commits.body:

  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.

_new_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
_new_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
_new_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
_new_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers

the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread

their text cannot drift from the verdict.

r_meta.title: Automated Reproducibility Checks for R Markdown Documents
r_meta.description_text: Provide reproducible R chunks in R Markdown document that automatically check computational results for reproducibility. This is achieved by creating json files storing metadata about computational results. A comprehensive tutorial to the package is available as preprint by Brandmaier & Peikert (2024, <doi:10.31234/osf.io/3zjvf>).

[Automated Reproducibility Testing in R Markdown](https://doi.org/10.1525/collabra.138638)


This package allows you to make computational results in R testable for reproduction (does the same script with the same data produce the same results, e.g. on a different computer and/or later in time). repos.readme_excerpt:
OIF (Output It Forward) is a Chrome extension that helps researchers detect and document open data indicators in scholarly articles while they browse. As you read a paper, OIF automatically scans the page for phrases and repository links commonly associated with open data practices, and logs matches to a running CSV file for systematic documentation.
OIF is designed with adaptability in mind: its phrase list and repository domain list are plain, editable text files, so tailoring the extension to your discipline requires no programming expertise, just edit a list.

Follow this link: https://chr

highlights.message: Give repository requests a stall guard; ask zip_peek for the exact central directory (0.3.3.15)
highlights.body:
- .mc_request(): httr2::request() with curl's low-speed limit (< 1 KB/s
  for 60 s) and a 30 s connect timeout, used by the 38 repository and
  database requests that had no time limit (zip listing, GitHub, GitLab,
  OSF, ResearchBox (300 s), PsychArchives, DSpace, AsPredicted, FSD,
  DataONE, Dryad, CrossRef, PubPeer, Retraction Watch, RegCheck status,

- zip_peek(): after a first tail too short for the central directory, the
  second request asks for the bytes the end record says it needs
  (.parse_zip_central_dir(need_only = TRUE)), up to 64 MB, instead of a
  fixed 1 MB

highlights.message: Stop the quadratic rescan of rejected blocks in .r_output_tables() (0.3.3.8)
highlights.body:
A printed data frame with no numeric column made every row start a new
scan of the rest of the print, so parsing console output grew with the
square of the rows (384 s for 1,000 rows, hours for 10,000). A rejected
block is now remembered: a later start inside it is only split when its
pattern of non-blank character positions differs from the last block
actually split, the only way its result can differ. Output is identical
on 113 cases; 1,000 rows take about 4 s. A progress line is printed
before each script's output is parsed.

Closes #483

highlights.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
highlights.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
highlights.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
highlights.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
highlights.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
highlights.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
highlights.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
highlights.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep one copy of each function defined twice in R/ (0.3.3.7)
highlights.body:
Eleven internal functions and one constant were defined twice; R loads R/
alphabetically, so one copy silently replaced the other. Kept: R/stat_helpers.R
for the nine statistics helpers and .STAT_PLACEHOLDERS (the file created as
their single home), omv.R for .html_inline_images(), reproducibility_check.R
for .repro_split_args(). All copies were identical, so behaviour is unchanged.
Each deleted copy leaves a one-line pointer to the kept one. New test fails
when any name is defined twice.

Closes #482
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Stop the quadratic character walks that hung reproducibility_check (0.3.3.6)
highlights.body:
Every place that walked text one character at a time with substr(x, i, i)
now splits the text into characters once and indexes the vector. For text
with a non-ASCII character substr() counts from the start on every call, so
the walk was quadratic: 201 s for a 200,000-character script, hours for a
1-MB one. Results are identical on 413 real R and Python scripts.

Changed: .repro_redirect_writes(), .repro_format_call_refs(),
.repro_split_args() (both copies), .repro_content_sniff(),
.r_call_object_ref(), .omv_extract_syntax(), .smcl_render_line().
repro_write_scripts() prints a line per script, so a slow rewrite can be
told apart from a hang.

Closes #481

highlights.message: Leave out and report all files that do not belong in a repository
highlights.body:
Extends the operating-system file filter to every file software creates by
itself that holds nothing a reader can use: operating-system files (macOS,
Windows, Linux desktops), RStudio's .Rproj.user/, Jupyter checkpoints,
compiled Python files and Office/LibreOffice lock files. Patterns from
GitHub's ignore-file templates, each also found in real repositories; files
that may matter (.RData, .Rhistory, backups, *.tmp, knitr caches) are kept.

repo_check and data_check leave them out of the file list; repo_check reports
them by kind in "Files that do not belong in the repository". The kind is
taken from the last path segment without basename(), which expanded a leading
"~" ("~$report.docx" became "Documents$report.docx").
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Support LDbase in repo_check; leave out operating-system files; warn on firewall browser checks (0.3.3.4)
highlights.body:
LDbase (ldbase.org, FSU's repository for educational and developmental
sciences) has no API, so the new ldbase_links()/ldbase_info() read its public
pages: links to projects, datasets, code and documents and 10.33009 DOIs are
found; a project's whole hierarchy (child projects included) is listed, each
item's current file in a folder named after the item, with the licence of
each item. Files download without an account. Pages are requested at most
once per second. Checked on 10 LDbase projects.

repo_check and data_check leave out files the operating system adds
(__MACOSX/, ._ files, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) and repo_check lists
them for the authors to remove: in one LDbase zip they were 993 of 1,826
listed files, and the ._ copies of .csv files were read as data.

A host's AWS WAF browser check (HTTP 202 + x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) now
gives a warning once per host; such files used to be skipped without a word
because their size could not be read.

DOIs under 10.33009 are no longer also looked up by dspace7_links();
open_practices counts "LDbase" as a repository word.

highlights.message: Python support fixes in reproducibility_check, %>% from other scripts, data_check and repo_check fixes (0.3.3.3)
highlights.body:
reproducibility_check (#479):
- Compare reported statistics with the analysis output once, after the R and
  the Python code, so Python output is included; Python-only papers keep the
  SPSS/Stata, self-reproducible-output and other-language sections and the
  SPSS/Stata red light
- Extract the code of Python notebooks and Quarto documents (and R-kernel
  notebooks) before running it
- Check Python syntax with ast.parse(); fall back to python3; report Python
  files as not run, instead of stopping, when no interpreter is found
- Install packages under their pip name (sklearn -> scikit-learn, ...)
- Require callr only for R code; drop the Python NameError re-run
- Return the summary as one text (two made the report error for R + Python)
- Stop exporting .repro_py_defined_vars(); correct help text and comments

R scripts that fail on %>% because packages are loaded in another script:
- A script another script runs with source() is only run inside that script
  (outcome run_by_source)
- Otherwise the re-run adds the library() calls of the project's other
  scripts, else the one package that exports the function, else magrittr;
  recorded in modifications and reported as reproducible after repair

Comparison with the paper: use the output's STATO type when a value's name is
not recognised (scipy's statistic/pvalue); type F_onewayResult,
PearsonRResult and Chi2ContingencyResult

data_check: warn on space-separated .csv files; keep the summary, report and
light when no table is readable (and return the column table as `table`);
read only the header line in the trial-level check (#477)

repo_check: ignore CI/service configuration files when deciding whether a
root-level R package is the deposit (#469)

reproducibility_check(workers > 1): copy all metacheck.* options into each
background process (#474)

check_file_naming(): help no longer lists case rules it does not check

Closes #479

Closes #477

highlights.message: Remove seq_endpoint(), seq_distance(), their *_df() versions, and seq_test_ranking()
highlights.body:
* They produced sequences of decimal strings for testing with the mappers, which no longer accept strings, so their default output failed there. Their essence is seq(from, to, by = 10^-digits).
* The "scrutiny" attribute loses name_test and seq_test, which only seq_test_ranking() read.
* Tests of other functions build their input with seq() piped into round() instead, and the devtools vignette covers only seq_disperse(). The GRIM oracle test pipes into round() as well.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Quiet the 0.6.1 install script and use a tibble in the benchmark
highlights.body: * install_scrutiny_0_6_1() tries CRAN's current packages before the archive and keeps the expected 404 from the other location quiet.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Leave the factory arguments out of the disabled-argument error
highlights.body: * Users of grimmer_map() and the like were told about .args_disabled and .args_fixed, which only matter to whoever created the mapper.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: List the removed mapper arguments and columns as breaking changes in NEWS
highlights.body: * The removal of debit_map(show_rec), grimmer_map(show_reason), debit_map()'s rounding column, and audit()'s fail_test2 moves from "Lifecycle updates" to "Function interfaces".
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Mark the percentage and sum tests as experimental
highlights.body: * is_percentage_of(), is_percentage_of_map(), is_percentage_of_map_seq(), add_up_to(), and add_up_to_map() carry the experimental badge, and NEWS and the vignette say so.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Hide the library(scrutiny) chunk and the header rule in vignettes
highlights.body:
* Every vignette still loads scrutiny, but in a chunk with include = FALSE.
* Article pages have no rule between the title and the text.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Correct NEWS claims and a stale comment from the recent cuts
highlights.body:
* GRIM's verdicts are unchanged only on testable value sets; untestable ones are now NA.
* .args_defaults never shipped, so NEWS no longer says it was replaced, and grim_map()'s items entry no longer claims the other mappers already kept n and items apart, which was only true of the dev version.
* A comment in grim_plot() still assumed grimmer_map() could omit the reason column.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a grim_plot_rates() study column named like a summary column
highlights.body: * A study column named observed, expected, value_sets, or ratio was overwritten by summarise(), so the study labels were lost without an error.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Check that function_map(.args_fixed) is a named list that overlaps nothing
highlights.body: * An unnamed value was passed to .fun by position, and a name shared with a by-row, helper, or disabled argument silently dropped that argument. Only overlap with key arguments was rejected.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Drop tolerance from grimmer_plot_values()
highlights.body:
* It passed tolerance to grimmer() on every call, so since grimmer(tolerance) was deprecated, each call warned. The function is new in 1.0.0, so the argument goes without a deprecation.
* The no-warnings test missed this because a deprecation warns once per session and an earlier test had used it up. It now sets lifecycle_verbosity = "warning".
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep the logo out of the first code chunk on pkgdown pages
highlights.body:
* The page header contains the right-floated logo, so the logo no longer hangs below the header line into the first code chunk.
* Copy buttons are always shown, faintly until hovered, instead of appearing only on hover.
* The copy tooltip opens to the left of the button, as pkgdown intends; it opened above it and covered the logo because Bootstrap 5 ignores pkgdown's Bootstrap 4 placement attribute.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Bring docs in line with the cut features
highlights.body:
* ?grim_map_seq no longer says that n is the sample size before multiplying in items, which no mapper does anymore.
* The pkgdown reference lists duplicate_detect() under "Deprecated" rather than "Superseded".
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Document the new tests and GRIM study-level tools in vignettes
highlights.body:
* A new vignette, "Percentages and sums", covers is_percentage_of() and add_up_to() with their mappers and audit() summaries.
* The GRIM vignette gains grim_plot_values() next to grim_plot(), and grim_binomial(), grim_binomial_power(), and grim_plot_rates() under GRIM statistics.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Cut the §2 dead weight and deprecate duplicate_detect()
highlights.body:
* Remove grim_ratio(), manage_key_colnames(), unnest_consistency_cols(), write_doc_factory_map_conventions(), and the rlang re-exports; unexport check_factory_dots(), check_args_disabled(), and decimal_places_scalar().
* Replace function_map(.args_defaults) by .args_fixed: values the factory-made function always passes on without exposing the argument. debit_map() loses show_rec and grimmer_map() loses show_reason; both outputs are always complete. debit_map() output loses its rounding column, which repeated the attribute, and audit() on GRIMMER output loses fail_test2, which could no longer be nonzero.
* duplicate_detect() warns with lifecycle; forensic_metascience calls it, so it stays for one more release.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Rewrite the handwritten-mapper section around the kept helpers
highlights.body: * The examples use absorb_key_args() for renaming key columns, which replaces the reference to manage_key_colnames(), and the requirements describe helper columns as returned rather than merged.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Stop multiplying items into n in grim_map() and grimmer_map()
highlights.body:
* A helper column is now returned as itself, right after the key columns, if it was given as an argument or a column. The n column is the sample size as given.
* This removes function_map(.cols_helper_merge), the scrutiny_cols_helper_merge attribute, and the code in function_map_seq() and function_map_total_n() that undid the merge before re-testing. grim_plot() already placed tiles at n * items.
* Breaking change for grim_map() and grimmer_map() output with items > 1.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
